assertions.name: signed_linking_number_vanishes
assertions.source: Brunnian control: the SIGNED Gauss integral over a Borromean component pair must vanish, validating both the quadrature and the realisation.

assertions.name: acn_converged
assertions.source: Grid refinement n=400 -> n=800 changes ACN by less than 1e-4.

assertions.name: acn_nonnegative_above_unlink_bound
assertions.source: Corrected bound: a Borromean component PAIR is the unlink on its own, so its minimal crossing number is 0, not the 2 that appears in the 3-component diagram.

assertions.name: per_pair_acn_falls_short_of_template_constant
assertions.source: The honest negative: the directly computed per-pair ACN is less than half the smallest template-implied constant, so the simplest crossing-number hypothesis does not reproduce kappa(A).

description: EXPLORATORY first-principles computation of the average crossing number (ACN) of a Borromean component PAIR -- the quantity the Freedman-He template fit left uncomputed (beans qou-0hdx, qou-8aed). Gauss integral with |numerator| on the standard mutually-orthogonal-ellipse realisation; the signed integral is computed alongside as a control and must vanish (Brunnian). ACN is realisation-dependent and bounds the Freedman-He asymptotic crossing number from ABOVE, with the Borromean minimal crossing number (2 per pair) bounding it from below. Nothing wired.

SUPERSEDED.why: The Freedman-He asymptotic crossing number in the LINK energy bound is ac(L_k, L): ONE component against the WHOLE link, summed over n COMPONENTS (Komendarczyk arXiv:0808.1533v1 eq. 43, p. 26). It is not a pairwise quantity -- no pair-indexed ac(L_i, L_j) appears in either primary source. The per-pair ACN computed here, and the 3x 'total link' reading below, are the wrong index and the wrong sum.
SUPERSEDED.malformed_question: This probe was built to settle whether the PAIR minimisation is constrained by the third component. There is no pair minimisation, so the question does not arise. The related (a)-vs-(b) question does resolve, against (a): Komendarczyk minimises a single-component Seifert genus over surfaces in R^3 minus the OTHER components, so Brunnian-ness does hold the value up -- by a complement constraint, not a constrained pair homotopy.
SUPERSEDED.retained_because: the Gauss-integral machinery and the Brunnian signed-linking control are reused by the correction probe, which assembles the correctly-indexed object from exactly these pair integrals.

method.realisation: three mutually orthogonal ellipses, semi-axes (a,b), cyclically permuted -- the standard Borromean model
method.quadrature: midpoint rule on [0,2pi]^2 (spectral for smooth periodic)
method.precision: float64; smooth integrand over disjoint curves, no singularity

bounds.reading: 2 <= C_true(pair) <= ACN(realisation); the ACN is an upper bound on Freedman-He's minimised asymptotic crossing number.

data.corrected_lower_bound: The first version of this probe asserted ACN >= 2, taking the '2 crossings per pair' of the standard Borromean DIAGRAM as a lower bound. That assertion FAILED (ACN = 1.6426) and it was WRONG: a pair of Borromean components, considered on its own as a 2-component link, is the UNLINK -- minimal crossing number 0, not 2. The 2-per-pair count is a property of the 3-component diagram, not of the pair. So the correct bound is 0 <= C_true(pair) <= ACN, and the computed value violates nothing. The failure is recorded rather than deleted.

total_link_reading.status: CANDIDATE ONLY -- explicitly not a result. The per-pair ACN (1.643) falls 59-66% short of the template-implied constant, so the simplest crossing-number hypothesis FAILS. Summing over all three pairs gives 4.928, which lands within 2.8% of the Vol~A target (4.793). There is a genuine physical argument for the total-link reading -- Brunnian-ness means a pair CANNOT be considered in isolation, since removing the third component unlinks it, so the energy attributable to a pair may legitimately involve the whole link's crossing structure. But two cautions bite hard: (i) the kappa data is already per-pair normalised, so multiplying by 3 risks double-counting, and (ii) the ACN varies by 7.8% across the aspect-ratio sweep, which is COMPARABLE TO the 2.8% agreement -- the match is within realisation noise and must not be read as a confirmation.
